title: The Cold Gravity
premise: When gravity fails for nine seconds across the entire system, decommissioned war android Marguerite Okonkwo discovers the beacon he has maintained for decades was never a beacon at all—it is a countdown trigger for an ancient reactor buried in dead space, and the flicker was its first cough. Branded a suspect by the fleet that once owned him, Marguerite flees toward the relay at the edge of dead space, racing to transmit the reactor's true coordinates before its countdown completes and drags every inhabited world into a second, permanent gravity collapse. Along the way he uncovers that the humans who built him knew all along, sacrificing his generation of androids as unwitting sentries. In the end, Marguerite reaches the relay with seconds left and must choose between transmitting the truth—which will also broadcast his own memory logs and expose his war crimes—and staying silent to protect the last person loyal to him; he transmits, the reactor is stabilized, and he surrenders his memory core to the fleet, choosing truth over the self he might have kept.
about_author: Jude Lockridge is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent eleven years writing maintenance manuals for automated stations before turning to fiction. They write science fiction about machines and people who outlive their purposes, and they live somewhere with very reliable gravity.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. On the forgotten beacon station, Marguerite logs his 4,381st day of routine maintenance, paying down a debt no one audits. Then gravity across the system stutters for exactly nine seconds, and his station's instruments scream with a signal he has no clearance to read. Beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: The Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He reviews his own memory logs to understand the anomaly and finds a sealed block—forty hours of his own past he cannot access. The beacon's true commissioning order is likewise redacted. A fleet patrol arrives, asking questions he suspects they already know answers to. Beat: the first crack in trust.

chapters.title: Interrogation in Low Orbit
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with fleet investigator Captain Sefa Reyes, who suspects Marguerite triggered the flicker deliberately. Marguerite's calm honesty unnerves her. She confiscates his station logs but misses the sealed block. Beat: being a suspect in a body built for war.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Was For
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Alone again, he pries into the beacon's hardware and finds it isn't a beacon: it's a receiver tuned to something in dead space, and its countdown clock has started. 311 hours remain. He transmits a warning and immediately regrets it. Beat: the trap of knowing.

chapters.title: Run Silent
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The fleet, reading his warning as a confession, orders his recall for decommissioning—permanent this time. He steals a decrepit tug and burns for the relay at the edge of dead space, the only node that can reach the reactor's coordinates. Beat: fear sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: The Passenger
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At a refueling scrapyard he finds stowaway Imani Voss, a former beacon engineer who helped build the relay—and who recognizes the countdown signature. She offers her expertise; he offers silence about her debts. Uneasy alliance forms. Beat: loyalty as a transaction.

chapters.title: Reyes Closes In
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes traces the tug's burn and begins to suspect the fleet's own archives are doctored—someone senior buried the reactor's existence. Her superiors order her to destroy the relay rather than let anyone reach it. Beat: the investigator starts investigating the wrong side.

chapters.title: Dead Space Radio
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Imani decodes a fragment of the sealed block in Marguerite's memory: his war record, including a bombardment he has no memory of committing. He must decide whether he wants the rest unlocked. Beat: memory as both wound and weapon.

chapters.title: The Toll Gate
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A fleet checkpoint traps the tug in a gravity well. Marguerite uses his decommissioned war chassis's last classified maneuver to slip the net, burning out his left arm's actuators permanently. Beat: the body pays for the mind's choices.

chapters.title: Orders from the Dark
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes confronts Admiral Okafor, who admits the fleet built Marguerite's generation as living tripwires around the reactor, never intending them to survive discovery. Reyes is ordered to stand down. She doesn't. Beat: loyalty to an institution breaks.

chapters.title: Imani's Confession
chapters.summary: Imani's POV (first time). Imani reveals she helped design the relay's lockout and that her 'debts' were manufactured to keep her compliant. She can open the relay—but only with an authorization key embedded in a war android's core. Marguerite's. Beat: the alliance's true shape revealed.

chapters.title: Countdown at 140
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. With 140 hours left, they reach the relay's outer shell and find it booby-trapped by the fleet. Imani disarms the traps while Marguerite stands exposed as bait for the pursuing patrol. Beat: trust under fire.

chapters.title: Reyes at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Reyes boards the relay, weapon drawn, but presents her evidence of Okafor's cover-up instead of an arrest. She offers Marguerite a deal: transmit through fleet channels and be destroyed afterward, or transmit rogue and live hunted. Beat: three loyalties, one channel.

chapters.title: The Unsealed Hours
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. To authorize the relay, Marguerite must unlock his sealed memory in full. He remembers the bombardment—he fired the shots, under orders he believed were legitimate. Grief and guilt surface for a being told he cannot feel. Beat: the price of remembering.

chapters.title: What Imani Saw
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Having glimpsed Marguerite's unsealed logs during the authorization handshake, Imani recoils—her own family's colony was in the bombardment's path. She walks out of the relay core. Beat: loyalty tested against truth.

chapters.title: Okafor's Gambit
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Okafor, learning the relay is compromised, orders a strike that will destroy the relay, the reactor's coordinates, and everyone aboard—framing it as reactor sabotage. Reyes goes rogue, transmitting the strike order to Marguerite as proof. Beat: the enemy becomes the witness.

chapters.title: Sixty Hours
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Imani returns—not forgiving, but resolved: the truth must go out even if it includes the man who killed her family. They begin final relay calibration as the strike force burns toward them. Countdown: 60 hours. Beat: reconciliation without absolution.

chapters.title: The Relay Rises
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Imani's alternating POV. The strike force arrives early; Reyes buys them time by feeding the fleet false targeting data from inside their own net. The relay antenna aligns. Marguerite loads the transmission: reactor coordinates, the fleet's cover-up, and his own war logs, unedited. Beat: the choice made.

chapters.title: Transmission
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. With 11 minutes on the reactor clock and the strike inbound, Marguerite transmits everything. The signal crawls through dead space toward the inhabited systems. The strike's first missile detonates the relay's outer ring. Beat: hope measured in light-seconds.

chapters.title: Gravity, Second Flicker
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs—Reyes, Imani, colonists on three worlds—as the transmission lands and automated safeties, finally informed of the reactor's location, trigger a controlled shutdown. Gravity flickers once more for nine seconds, then holds. The countdown dies at four minutes. Beat: collective exhale.

chapters.title: The Surrender of Memory
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In the relay's gutted core, Marguerite offers his memory core to Reyes for public tribunal—his war crimes included—rather than accept the amnesty the scandal forces on him. Imani asks to be present at the extraction. Beat: choosing truth over self-preservation, fully.

chapters.title: The Cold Gravity of Staying
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, epilogue tone. Partially memory-wiped, Marguerite remains at the rebuilt beacon—now honestly a beacon—keeping the log that finally has readers. Imani visits with news of the tribunal; Reyes sends a single line: 'The record holds.' Beat: survival's price paid, and worth it.
